description: A station-level table from the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, published on the Open Data NY portal, of the New York City subway stations where Wi-Fi and commercial cell service were available underground. The MTA contracted Transit Wireless to provide Wi-Fi and cell service in all underground stations; service began in 2011 and reached all of them in January 2017. Contents: 283 rows, each with station name, station complex, lines, a historic-station flag, borough, county, latitude and longitude, whether Wi-Fi is available and separate yes or no flags for AT&T, Sprint, T-Mobile and Verizon service. Coverage: New York City subway stations, as a snapshot for part of 2015 and 2016. Format and access: free download or query through the Socrata API in CSV, JSON and other formats; the portal marks it static and not updated, with rows last changed in December 2021. Licence and cost: free; no licence is named in the dataset metadata, so the portal's terms of use apply. Caveats: a historical snapshot from before full build-out, with station points, not coverage footprints inside tunnels, and Sprint has since merged into T-Mobile. Useful for cascading failure and emergency response studies that need to know where riders and staff could call or connect underground, and which carriers a station depended on. No closely related telecom coverage record for transit was found in the catalogue.
